boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented George Fox rituals, recurring events and campus spectacles—from passing a presidential coin to plunging into Hess Creek.

cards.title: Pass the Promise Forward
cards.subtitle: A graduating student thanks someone who made them feel known
cards.notes: Keep the coin until your final semester, then present it to a George Fox mentor, professor, staff member or community member.
cards.short_summary: A keepsake changes hands as a personal thank-you for being seen, valued and known.
cards.evidence_claim: George Fox launched this tradition in 2025; graduating students are invited to present a Presidential Challenge Coin to someone who made them feel known during their university journey.
cards.access_notes: Students receive or collect coins through designated university ceremonies or campus offices; alumni participation requires purchasing a coin.

cards.title: Wait for Bruin Jr. to Flash
cards.subtitle: A century-old scramble for a stuffed bear
cards.notes: Watch only from the designated spectator area unless organizers authorize participation; current brawls are prearranged and supervised.
cards.short_summary: The sudden appearance of Bruin Jr. launches George Fox’s strangest organized contest.
cards.evidence_claim: George Fox documents Bruin Brawl as a tradition dating to the late 1890s in which the appearance of Bruin Jr. starts a contest for possession; current brawls are prearranged and supervised.
cards.access_notes: Participate only through the university-organized, supervised event and follow all event rules, releases and staff directions.

cards.title: Finish in Every Color
cards.subtitle: A campus race with airborne color and popsicles
cards.notes: Wear the issued event shirt, follow the marked campus route and use the water stations before joining music and popsicles at the finish.
cards.short_summary: Runners begin in clean shirts and complete the campus course covered in thrown color.
cards.evidence_claim: George Fox Student Activities identifies Color Run as a campus tradition featuring a race around campus, thrown colors, water stations, music and popsicles at the finish.
cards.access_notes: Check the current Student Activities calendar for the event date and participation instructions; protect eyes and follow organizer guidance.

cards.title: Start the Year in Neon
cards.subtitle: Leg warmers meet the historic Wood-Mar wall
cards.notes: Build an ’80s-inspired outfit, arrive at the EHS Atrium at the posted time and expect dancing, snacks and limited themed giveaways.
cards.short_summary: The first dance of the year fills the EHS Atrium with retro clothes, music and movie-character costumes.
cards.evidence_claim: George Fox describes the '80s Dance as the first dance of the year, held in the EHS Atrium with period-inspired clothing, music, snacks and themed giveaways.
cards.access_notes: Attendance details and venue access depend on the current Student Activities announcement; limited giveaways are not guaranteed.

cards.title: Line Dance Across the Quad
cards.subtitle: Flannel, field games and a mechanical bull
cards.notes: Wear clothes suitable for outdoor games, join the line dancing or sack races and follow staff instructions before trying the mechanical bull.
cards.short_summary: A country-styled quad gathering combines live music, games, seasonal snacks and line dancing.
cards.evidence_claim: George Fox lists Fox Jamboree among its traditions and describes a quad event with a live band, line dancing, games, food and a mechanical bull.
cards.access_notes: Check the current event notice for weather, eligibility and activity rules; use the mechanical bull only under event supervision.

cards.title: End the Semester Off Campus
cards.subtitle: A long-running Portland-area ballroom dance
cards.notes: Watch Student Activities for registration and transportation details, then dress for an evening of dancing, desserts and photo-booth pictures.
cards.short_summary: Students close the semester with a formal dance staged at a ballroom in the Portland area.
cards.evidence_claim: George Fox calls Winter Formal a long-running campus tradition held annually at an off-campus ballroom in the Portland area, with desserts, a photo booth and dancing.
cards.access_notes: The ballroom and attendance process can change annually; confirm registration, transportation and guest rules in the current announcement.

cards.title: Tell a Story Without Singing
cards.subtitle: Auditioned group routines take the stage
cards.notes: Form a group and follow the published audition process, or attend as an audience member to watch the selected story-driven routines.
cards.short_summary: Teams combine choreography, costumes and recorded music in an auditioned campus showcase.
cards.evidence_claim: George Fox presents Lip Sync as a traditional group dance-off whose performing groups complete an audition process before taking the stage.
cards.access_notes: Performers must use the current audition process; spectators should check Student Activities for the venue, date and entry details.

cards.title: Compete for a Pantry Crown
cards.subtitle: A pageant benefiting the Bruin Community Pantry
cards.notes: Attend to support the contestants and campus pantry, or follow the current application process if Student Activities opens contestant spots.
cards.short_summary: A personality-centered pageant turns a novelty crown into support for George Fox’s food bank.
cards.evidence_claim: George Fox identifies Mr. Bruin as a pageant in which male students compete for a crown while raising funds for the university’s Bruin Community Pantry.
cards.access_notes: Check the current event announcement for contestant eligibility, audience admission and donation arrangements.

cards.title: Earn the Hess Creek Sweatshirt
cards.subtitle: A cold-water plunge followed by fire and s’mores
cards.notes: Register before spaces fill, bring dry layers and enter Hess Creek only during the organized event under staff safety instructions.
cards.short_summary: A brief winter dip earns participants a collectible sweatshirt and a warm finish by the bonfire.
cards.evidence_claim: George Fox describes Polar Plunge as a limited-capacity Hess Creek plunge followed by music, s’mores and a bonfire, with participants receiving a Polar Plunge sweatshirt.
cards.access_notes: Advance signup is required and space is limited; enter the creek only during the supervised university event and follow all safety directions.

cards.title: Pause Finals for Pancakes
cards.subtitle: Study Day ends with breakfast food and a movie
cards.notes: Look for the finals-week announcement, then bring student identification if requested and take a study break on the night of Study Day.
cards.short_summary: George Fox marks the start of finals with a nighttime breakfast and movie for students.
cards.evidence_claim: George Fox states that Late Night Breakfast occurs on the night of Study Day at the beginning of finals week and is free for all students.
cards.access_notes: The official page confirms the event occurs at night on Study Day; verify the current semester’s exact time and location with Student Activities.
